static_traits.name: Wen David
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends who understand the love of animals, but finds it less easy to connect with people than with animals, and struggles to talk about feelings of inadequacy with friends
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet experienced similar psychological problems; no history of psychotherapy; no obvious physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent thinking, high cooperativeness; tending to focus on the unfinished and inadequacy, difficulty internalizing positive feedback (negating the positive, mental filtering)

basic_info.main_problem: I often visit animal shelters and work closely with animals, but I persistently feel I am not doing enough for the local community. These feelings have persisted for the past few months and have affected my daily activities and thinking.
basic_info.core_demands: What prompted me to seek counseling this time is the overwhelming feeling of 'not doing enough', which has begun to affect my daily life and mental health.
growth_experiences: Once rescued a sick puppy with the team, and after several months of care it was finally adopted by a loving family; it was regarded at the time as 'a good day', but the client still evaluates it as 'just a small victory'.

core_beliefs: My contributions are not enough / I am not valuable enough
Only when the overall situation changes significantly do my efforts count

special_situations.event: Every time they visit the animal shelter and see that there are still many animals needing rescue
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot significantly reduce suffering or solve big problems, it means I am not doing enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Increasing volunteer hours and donating supplies to compensate for feelings of inadequacy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am still not doing enough / my efforts are just a drop in the ocean

special_situations.event: The shelter staff thanked me for my help and recognized my work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless I see a huge improvement in the overall situation, positive feedback does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores affirmation and continues to raise demands on herself
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This gratitude is just empty talk; I still have not done enough

special_situations.event: Recalling those animals that have not yet been rescued or whose conditions have not yet improved
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as there is still one individual not yet rescued, my efforts are a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly ruminates and plans to invest more time and energy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I still cannot help them; I am failing

special_situations.event: Thinking about widespread community-level problems and unmet needs
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should take personal responsibility for the community's suffering
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Takes pressure and responsibility onto oneself, compensating by giving more
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not solve these problems, I am letting the community down

core_conflict.wish: Longs to make a meaningful contribution and be recognized, gaining an inner sense of value and satisfaction
core_conflict.fear: Fearing I am not good enough, worthless, and unable to stop the ongoing suffering
defense_goal: Maintaining high standards and self-reproach to alleviate the anxiety of 'worthlessness'
Gains a sense of control and relieves guilt by doubling his investment

object_relations.object_representation: The community/others are a never-ending source of needs and suffering

object_relations.self_representation: A caregiver who finds connecting with others relatively difficult
object_relations.object_representation: Others find it hard to understand one's feelings; positive feedback seems hollow

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or shelter staff gives positive feedback and recognizes contributions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interpreting positive feedback as unreal 'empty talk', insufficient to prove one's worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Persisting in downplaying praise, repeating 'still not enough', in a flat but firm tone, avoiding elaboration of emotional experiences.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes 'changing perspective / viewing in a balanced way' and invites her to attend to the achievements already made
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing this as making oneself ignore the real problems, feeling it is insincere, thus keeping distance
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using abstract expressions like 'the big picture' and 'in theory' to rebut, maintaining an objectively detached tone and logical explanations.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking of animals not yet rescued or unmet community needs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning uncontrollable external outcomes into self-blame, seeing them as personal inadequacy and failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing personal inadequacy in a self-critical tone; reducing help-seeking or outward expression.

manifestations: Persistently feeling not doing enough for the community
Difficulty internalizing positive feedback from others
Focusing on the unfinished and suffering while overlooking small victories
Repeatedly thinking about what more they could do
outcomes: Hard to focus on the present and gain satisfaction when interacting with animals at the shelter

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently demands inwardly with 'should / must do more'
Treats the external standard that only macro-level change counts as a contribution as a condition of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Finding it difficult to talk about feelings of inadequacy with friends; turning stress and self-blame against the self
At the shelter, keeps tension and self-criticism to themselves, reducing direct expression with people

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, involving excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly evaluating whether one has done enough; persistent self-doubt
Expresses needs and emotions cautiously; hard to receive positive feedback

exception_events.target_problem: In situations of rescuing animals at shelters or interacting with pets, the client typically falls into rumination of 'I am not doing enough' and self-doubt, struggling to experience a sense of achievement, affecting focus and daily activities.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once helped a sickly puppy, after months of care it was adopted by a loving family; that day was regarded by the client as a 'good day', seeing concrete change and results.
exception_events.reason: Clue: the care invested over a long term produced visible results; positive feedback and support from the adoptive family and the shelter team; the success of specific cases made them briefly focus on the contributions already made.

positive_force: Stable professional skills and identity (PhD in veterinary medicine)
Continuous volunteer service and material donations, with a sense of responsibility and altruistic motivation
Ability to build connections with animals and devote to long-term care
Positive feedback and recognition given by shelter staff
Has had the experience of successfully rescuing and seeing concrete change (a puppy being adopted)
negative_force: Mental filtering and negating the positive; difficulty internalizing affirmation
Personalizing community problems, attributing macro suffering to one's own responsibility
High-pressure worth condition: only a 'huge change' counts as a contribution
Relatively difficult to connect with people; difficulty expressing feelings of inadequacy; limited mobilization of social support
Persistent rumination and self-blame, affecting attention and daily activities

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent self-denial and rumination ('I am not doing enough') when in contact with animals or visiting shelters
antecedent: Every visit to the animal shelter
Receiving thanks and positive feedback from staff
Considering unmet needs and suffering at the community level
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjection's high standards and cognitive biases (mental filtering, negating the positive, personalization) lead to building self-worth on macro-level change, seeing unmet needs as personal failure.
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a sense of responsibility and driving more investment through self-pressure, while avoiding satisfaction and comfort to reduce guilt and feelings of unworthiness.
target_behavior.consequence: Moderate stress and self-doubt; difficulty focusing on the present; daily activities and thinking affected; work not yet significantly impaired, but the quality of subjective experience declines.
